test_policy.notes: International freshman page lists SAT/ACT scores as optional (submit to institution code 6917). Domestic first-time students qualify for assured admission by meeting ONE of: 2.5 unweighted GPA, SAT 980 / ACT 19, or top 50% of class; a Student Success Plan route admits 2.0-2.49 GPA, SAT 940 / ACT 18 or top 50%. International applicants need a 2.0 of 4.0 GPA (converted by the International Programs staff).

requirements.notes: Apply through ApplyTexas (international application); the $25 fee is non-refundable (the first-time-in-college page says a fee waiver may be available; eligibility is not stated for international students). International applicants also submit official secondary school records (with English translation), proof of English proficiency, an F-1 Student Agreement Form, a Letter of Financial Sponsorship plus bank statements covering one year of cost of attendance, and a passport copy. Essays and recommendations are not required for international freshmen.

deadlines.label: International priority deadline, fall 2027 (students outside the U.S.)
deadlines.notes: The page prints 'June 15th' with no year, so June 15, 2027 is assumed for fall 2027 entry. Complete application and documents must be received by this date to guarantee a decision. June 15 is also the international scholarship deadline for fall.

deadlines.label: Last date to apply for fall 2027 (students outside the U.S.)
deadlines.notes: Students may apply until July 15th; applications after the priority date are reviewed case by case. The year is not printed, so 2027 is assumed. U.S.-based international transfer students have an Aug 18 fall deadline. Spring entry: priority Nov 15, apply until Dec 10.

deadlines.label: International Merit Scholarship application, fall 2027
deadlines.notes: The year is not printed, so June 15, 2027 is assumed. The student must already be admitted and both the general scholarship application and the international merit application must be complete.

english_policy.waiver_notes: Required for students whose native language is not English or whose instruction was not in English. Exempt: citizens of listed native-English countries, applicants with a U.S. high school diploma or degree, applicants who finished freshman English composition with C+ or better, and those with higher education completed at an English-medium institution verified by a NACES member. Others can request a waiver through a Listening, Speaking and Writing assessment with the International Programs office. Scores must be less than 3 years old.

english.notes: Internet-based minimum 61; paper-based minimum 500. Institution code 6917.
The page names Duolingo first and says the university requires 85 or higher.

Cambridge English Level B1 or higher; no numeric score is given. Other accepted proofs: iTEP 3.5, SAT 1100 (Reading+Math), ACT 18, MELAB 69, WASSCE/WAEC C4 in English, completion of a CEA-accredited English program.

aid.notes: International Student Merit Scholarship: for F-1 students it applies the in-state tuition rate and can reduce the cost of attendance by $3,000 to $10,000 over two semesters (tuition and fees only; essay and resume required; apply by June 15 for fall; keep 2.5 GPA and 10 volunteer hours). International Student Cultural Scholarship: $1,500 per year ($750 per semester) for F-1/J-1 students on first-come basis, applied to out-of-state tuition and fees; a student can hold only one international scholarship. Need-based aid for international students is not stated.

cost.notes: Schedule of charges 2026-27, 12 credit hours per semester doubled to a year: resident tuition $2,555.28 per semester; non-resident and international tuition $7,691.28 per semester; fees $337.44 service + $585.60 extended access + $96.00 library per semester. The cost-of-attendance page shows a higher all-in figure for tuition and fees ($21,607 per year out-of-state/international, $8,767 in-state), which includes charges not itemized in the schedule. Housing and food, books, other costs (transportation $1,425 plus miscellaneous $2,371) and the total cost of attendance come from the dorm column of that page's out-of-state/international per-year table. Freshmen must live on campus; the 2024-25 international cost page also lists mandatory F-1 health insurance of $3,147
